subject: Post-call action plan: inference fit and SLA constraints for Stratagem Labs
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@stratagemlabs.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: priya@stratagemlabs.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-14T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: today’s discovery — throughput & tail latency

Thanks for the run-through this morning — appreciate you and Kim taking the time. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned and to surface a few follow-ups before the tech deep-dive: 

Pain points we confirmed:
- Production tail latency (p95/p99) spikes under burst traffic; impacts user experience for real-time payments flows.
- Current infra cost per inference has variability we can’t justify as we scale to 100k DAU.
- Ops team lacks visibility into model-level token cost and routing behavior across regions.

Goals / success criteria (high level):
- p95 text generation latency <= 220ms for median prompt (50–120 tokens).
- Sustained burst throughput ~120 req/s with 2x short bursts up to 300 req/s for 5–10s windows without SLA failures.
- Predictable per-token cost (<$0.0009/token equivalent) and clear fallback behavior to cheaper variants during heavy load.

Model requirements we mentioned: fine-tuned 7B family for NLU + 70B class for longer summaries (cold path). Most traffic will hit the 7B path; a subset (~8%) will require the 70B model. Typical prompt lengths: 25–150 tokens; response lengths 40–250 tokens.

Attachments I’m sending with this note: stratagem_traffic_profile.csv (sample 48h traffic), prompt_set_v1.json (P0 prompts + expected outputs).

Open questions we didn’t close:
- Tokenization details you need from our side (we used UTF-8 / whitespace + punctuation for metrics).
- Which quantized model families Redwood recommends for our p95 targets (mixed-precision quant vs int8?).
- If you can sketch an initial canary plan for Dedicated vs Hosted fallback.

Next steps we’d like from Redwood: topology sketch, rough cost estimate for Dedicated reserved baseline (monthly), and a short canary plan for a phased rollout. Happy to run a quick synchronous deep-dive next week — Wed/Thu mornings PT preferred.

—Samir
Stratagem Labs — Head of Product
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@stratagemlabs.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-14T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: today’s discovery — throughput & tail latency

Thanks Samir — appreciate the crisp summary and attachments. Confirming receipt of stratagem_traffic_profile.csv and prompt_set_v1.json. Below is our working recap, assumptions, and a proposed topology for the first pass. Please consider this a living doc — we’ll refine after the technical deep-dive.

Redwood assumptions (please confirm or correct):
- Traffic profile: 120 req/s steady with 5–10s bursts to 300 req/s (matches CSV).
- Token distributions: median 80 tokens in + ~120 tokens out for primary paths; heavy-tail to 400 tokens combined.
- 8% of requests require the 70B variant; 92% should be serviceable by a 7B family fine-tune.

Initial topology recommendation (MVP canary):
- Phase 0 (hosted): run 7B quantized (int8/4-bit mixed) on Hosted for steady-state traffic with autoscaling pools and prefix KV caching for repeated prompts.
- Phase 1 (dedicated reserve): spin up Dedicated GPU pool (2x node types) in primary region with multi-zone placement for resilience; reserve capacity sized for baseline 150 req/s with burst headroom using rapid autoscaler to handle 300 req/s short bursts.
- Fallbacks: smart routing policy to an economical 7B-quant variant under overload and synchronous fallback to a cached summary response if the 70B path is saturated.
- Observability: token-level cost numbers, p95/p99 latency per-route, per-model KV hit rates, and a canary dashboard.

Performance levers we’ll tune: batching window (20–60ms), dynamic KV caching TTLs, adaptive quantization (mixed-precision for 70B cold path), and request-level routing by latency vs cost SLO.

Outstanding technical questions for your infra team:
1) Can you share real request concurrency (concurrent users) vs requests/sec in sample windows? The CSV helps but we need concurrency to size KV cache and connection pools.
2) Are there any hard encryption/KMS constraints for cold model artifacts (HSM requirement)?
3) Do you have a strict max cold-start penalty (how long can a 70B cold-start be before it’s considered an SLA violation)?

Quick ask: are Wed 6/16 9:30am PT or Thu 6/17 10:00am PT good for a 45-minute technical deep-dive (we’ll bring infra + runtime engs)? I’ll attach a short topology sketch (redwood_mvp_topology_sketch.pdf) and a proposed Mutual Action Plan after we align.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Reddy <priya@stratagemlabs.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.k@stratagemlabs.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: today’s discovery — throughput & tail latency

Thanks Sean — Wed 6/16 9:30am PT works for us, confirmed. Quick answers to your questions below and a couple of notes from our security/compliance lead: 

Answers / clarifications:
- Concurrency: typical concurrency (panel users) is ~40–60 concurrent sessions during steady load; bursts push concurrency to ~140 for 5–12s windows.
- KMS/HSM: we do require encryption-at-rest for model artifacts with a customer-managed KMS for production Dedicated deployments. Hosted PoC can use Redwood-managed keys if needed for an initial canary.
- Cold-start tolerance: for the 70B path we need cold-starts to be <4s for the user-facing flow; anything longer must trigger a graceful degraded path.

Security asks (short):
- Can you share SOC 2 type II readiness evidence and data retention options ahead of the deep-dive?
- Also attach a sample minimal network diagram for VPC peering if we move to Dedicated (we’ll share firewall requirements).

I’ve attached prompt_set_v1.json and an augmented traffic CSV (stratagem_traffic_profile.csv) with concurrency annotations. We’ll have our infra lead Alex on the call Wed to cover KMS and peering requirements.

—Priya
Infrastructure Lead, Stratagem Labs
